# Floating tables in independent sections

These original controls are generated by `tools/section_floating_tables_fixture.py`
from the repository-authored `multipage-floating/text-480-15.docx` control. No
corpus content or embedded font programs are included. Each copy retains the
same table, text, positioning and page geometry.

`separate.docx` places the two copies in next-page sections. The expected four
pages compose the existing two-page native reference twice; that
specification-based composition check remains separate. A fresh native reference export
now independently confirms the composite itself has four pages.
`reference.json` records its 42 horizontal text lines and 260 non-whitespace
character origins, source/PDF hashes and export provenance. PDF-declared Unicode
and text operators were read with FontFile/FontFile2/FontFile3 excluded before
font construction. No font programs or native PDF are distributed. The source
bytes and the reference application's saved state were unchanged. Browser checks
compare all wrapped text segments with the existing 0.15-point horizontal and
0.2-point baseline tolerances and exercise editing on the final continuation
page, export/reopen, untouched package parts and exact undo. The fresh native
comparison checks every captured character at those same tolerances.

`continuous.docx` joins the copies using a continuous section break; `same.docx`
puts both tables in one section. Numeric-position tables that permit overlap now
render in both shared-flow combinations. Each has three native pages. Flows with
prohibited table overlap retain the collision guard and remain required work.

Fresh native shared-flow references (2026-10-05): `same-reference.json` and
`continuous-reference.json` independently record reference-application UI
exports of exact owned copies. Each has three pages, 42 horizontal text lines
and 260 non-whitespace character origins. The reference application permits these tables to overlap
on the middle page: the first table's continuation and the next table's initial
fragment coexist. Following regular paragraphs wrap around the fragments.
The source bytes remain unchanged; the visible Saved to this PC title and
disabled Undo were checked before and after Export/Create PDF. Native PDFs stay
private. The metadata reader excludes font programs before font construction.

The implementation matches every recorded character at the existing 0.15-point
horizontal and 0.2-point baseline tolerances. Browser checks also cover shared-flow
editing, exact package/paint undo and exported/reopened paint. All 368 original
documents and 916 pages retain their pre-edit RGBA and structural results. All
five section merges in the chemistry original preserve unrelated parts and undo
printed pixels exactly. These checks do not establish whole-corpus native fidelity
or global latency bounds. Flows prohibiting overlap still need collision-resolution
coverage. No reference/specification divergence is claimed.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.6.17–18 define section-property ownership, §17.6.22 and
§17.18.77 define section starts, and §17.4.57 defines floating-table positioning.
Next-page sections have independent body flows; continuous sections may share
one sheet. This change does not claim a reference/specification divergence.

To regenerate only the native metadata, export the exact unchanged control
from its already-opened visible reference-application instance, retaining its source hash and
saved-state observations, then run `tools/record_section_floating_native.py`
with the private PDF, ownership-state JSON and reference output path. The tool
rejects unverified source bytes or state and leaves its inputs untouched.
Pass `--source` for a different independently authored control; all ownership,
hash and state requirements still apply.
